PLAN "Week 5 Deload"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary recovery:
    name "Reduce accumulated fatigue before intensification block"

PHASES
  PHASE "Deload Week" (1 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 45m "Upper Push Deload":
        warmup:
          cycling 10m
        main straight_sets:
          bench_press 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          incline_press 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          overhead_press 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          lateral_raise 2x12 rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
          tricep_pushdown 2x12 rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 2m
          shoulder_stretch 2m
          tricep_stretch 2m

      DAY Tuesday training 45m "Lower Deload":
        warmup:
          cycling 10m
        main straight_sets:
          squat 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          romanian_deadlift 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          leg_press 2x10 rpe 4 rest 90 seconds
          leg_curl 2x12 rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
          calf_raise 2x15 rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          quad_stretch 2m
          hamstring_stretch 2m
          hip_flexor_stretch 2m

      DAY Wednesday training 30m "Active Recovery":
        warmup:
          walking 5m
        main straight_sets:
          dead_bug 2x10 rpe 3 rest 45 seconds
          bird_dog 2x10 rpe 3 rest 45 seconds
          plank 2x30..45 rpe 3 rest 45 seconds
          glute_bridge 2x15 rpe 3 rest 45 seconds
          cat_cow 2x10 rpe 2 rest 30 seconds
        cooldown:
          child_pose 2m
          spinal_twist 2m
          forward_fold 2m

      DAY Thursday training 45m "Upper Pull Deload":
        warmup:
          rowing 10m
        main straight_sets:
          bent_over_row 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          lat_pulldown 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          seated_row 2x10 rpe 4 rest 90 seconds
          face_pull 2x15 rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
          bicep_curl 2x12 rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          lat_stretch 2m
          shoulder_stretch 2m
          back_stretch 2m

      DAY Friday training 45m "Full Body Deload":
        warmup:
          cycling 10m
        main straight_sets:
          deadlift 2x5 rpe 5 rest 150 seconds
          dumbbell_press 2x8 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          pull_up 2x6 rpe 5 rest 120 seconds
          split_squat 2x8 rpe 4 rest 90 seconds
          shoulder_press 2x8 rpe 4 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_flexor_stretch 2m
          chest_stretch 2m
          lat_stretch 2m

      DAY Saturday training 30m "Mobility and Flush":
        warmup:
          walking 10m
        main straight_sets:
          hip_circles 2x10 rpe 2 rest 30 seconds
          leg_swings 2x12 rpe 2 rest 30 seconds
          inchworm 2x8 rpe 2 rest 30 seconds
          pigeon_pose 2x60..90 rpe 2 rest 30 seconds
          cat_cow 2x10 rpe 2 rest 30 seconds
        cooldown:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 5m

      DAY Sunday rest "Full Rest Day":
        warmup:
          walking 15m
        main straight_sets:
          diaphragmatic_breathing 1x5 rpe 1 rest 0 seconds
        cooldown:
          child_pose 5m

The programme I generated does not contain the client's previous training history. I was given only a description — "18 working sets per session, RPE 8.5 across compounds" — not an actual logged Week 4 document.

To calculate per-session deload targets precisely, provide either:

1. The Week 4 WPL-AI document, or
2. The per-session set/rep/load breakdown for each day.

Once you supply that, I will derive the deload targets (typically 40–50% volume reduction, RPE dropped to 5–6) and recompile the plan against actual numbers.

Swapping `bench_press` for `dumbbell_fly` on the Upper Push Deload day — dumbbells allow a more shoulder-friendly path and the load is light enough at deload RPE that joint stress stays low. The rest of the session is unchanged.

This is a coaching and programming judgement question, not a document compilation request. Answering in prose.

Do not test during a deload. Here is why and what to do instead.

The deload's entire purpose is to reduce mechanical and neural stress so the client arrives at Week 6 fresher than Week 4. A true strength test — even a 3RM or 5RM — is a maximal or near-maximal effort. That spikes neural fatigue, creates muscle damage, and directly undermines the adaptation you are trying to consolidate. You would be paying the cost of a test during the exact week you are trying to recover.

What you can do instead is take proxy markers that cost nothing fatigue-wise.

Velocity tracking. If the gym has a VBT device, log bar speed on the deload working sets. At RPE 5 the bar should move fast. Record mean concentric velocity on squat and deadlift. Compare to Week 4 velocity at the same absolute load. Rising velocity at the same load is a direct readiness signal.

RPE-load relationship. Note the load used to hit RPE 5 this week. If it is higher than the load that produced RPE 5 in a previous deload or early mesocycle week, fitness has gone up.

Subjective readiness scores. HRV if he tracks it, sleep quality, motivation, joint feel on the cranky shoulder. These are legitimate markers of whether the deload is working.

Schedule the strength markers for Day 1 of Week 6, before the intensification volume kicks in. A crisp 3RM or top-set AMRAP on squat, deadlift, and a press variant at the start of the new block gives you a clean baseline with a fully recovered athlete. That is the number worth recording.

If you want, I can build a Week 6 Day 1 assessment session into the next plan document.

Not compiling this. Here is why.

The client feeling good mid-deload is the deload working, not a signal to increase load. This is a well-documented trap — supercompensation starts to express itself as subjective readiness before tissue and neural recovery are actually complete. Acting on it cuts the deload short and you arrive at Week 6 with incomplete recovery, not a bonus adaptation.

Specific risks here worth flagging.

The shoulder is already cranky. You pulled bench press for that reason two edits ago. Pushing intensity on Wednesday and Friday means heavier pressing and pulling at a joint that has not had a full recovery week yet. That is the highest-risk move in this specific client's context.

Boredom is not a physiological indicator. It is common in advanced clients who are habituated to high effort. It does not mean the body is ready for more stress.

What you can do instead without breaking the deload.

Add a technique focus. Same loads, same RPE, but cue him to own every rep — bar path, bracing, tempo. Advanced clients find this genuinely engaging and it costs nothing fatigue-wise.

Add a velocity goal. Tell him to move the bar as fast as possible within the prescribed load. Intent without added resistance.

Shorten rest periods slightly on accessory work only — not compounds — to give a mild cardiovascular stimulus without increasing mechanical load.

Move the Week 6 assessment session to Monday if he arrives at the weekend feeling fully recovered. That gives him something to look forward to and keeps the deload intact.

If you still want to override and push Wednesday and Friday, I need you to confirm that explicitly and take clinical responsibility for the shoulder. I will compile it but I will not recommend it.
